name: Sterling-Nakamura Holographic Business Card HBC-1
description: A credit-card-sized device that projects a small holographic display containing the owner's identity information, professional credentials, and an encrypted contact protocol. The HBC-1 is Sterling-Nakamura's standard-issue networking tool for corporate personnel — when two HBC-1 cards are brought within 5 cm of each other, they exchange encrypted identity packets and establish a secure communication channel between the owners' Diaspora profiles. The holographic display can be customized with corporate branding, animated logos, and interactive elements. What makes the HBC-1 notable in security circles is that its exchange protocol has been exploited to deliver malware payloads — a handshake with a modified HBC-1 can inject code directly into the recipient's Diaspora profile.
story_hooks: A weaponized HBC-1 was used to deliver a Diaspora profile exploit during a networking event — every person who exchanged cards with the attacker had their secure communications compromised.
A collection of HBC-1 cards found at a crime scene contains encrypted data packets that, when assembled in sequence, form a complete intelligence dossier on a corporate target.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek credit-card-sized device with a mirror-black front face that serves as a holographic emitter. The surface appears perfectly flat until activated, at which point a faint shimmer indicates the projection field. The card stock itself has a subtle iridescence, catching light with hints of deep blue and silver. Despite its slim profile, the device feels substantial and precision-engineered.
physical_description.dimensions: Standard credit card format: 85.6 × 53.98 mm, approximately 2.8 mm thick
physical_description.weight_description: Pocketable — weighs virtually nothing (10 grams), easily carried in wallet, cardholder, or suit jacket
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade composite polymer with embedded holographic projection layer and NFC coil matrix
physical_description.finish: Matte black front surface with mirror-polished beveled edges; subtle brushed metal backing with Sterling-Nakamura branding
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominantly black and gunmetal gray with accent lines of electric blue along the top edge; holographic projections render in full color with cyan-to-purple gradients
physical_description.interface_elements: Single recessed activation button (top-right corner), minimal visible electronics; holographic display projects 5cm above surface showing name, title, credentials, and animated corporate logo; faint indicator LED (blue when active, amber when in pairing mode)
distinctive_features: Holographic projection field creates floating 3D text and animated company branding
Micro-etched serial number on backing plate
Hairline groove around perimeter indicating modular construction
Soft glow emanating from internal projection chamber when activated
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Sterling-Nakamura corporate logo (stylized SN cipher) centered on backing; regulatory compliance stamps (GLMZ certification, QUANTA-encrypted); QR code for Diaspora profile link etched in corner
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine corporate condition — rarely shows wear due to protective materials; in use, a faint blue aura surrounds the card during data exchange, and the holographic display flickers slightly during handshake protocols
